summary: Harker panics on realising he is a prisoner, then resolves to keep his fears hidden and his eyes open. He watches the Count make his bed and lay the table, and so deduces there are no servants and that the Count himself drove the calèche. The Count talks proudly of the Szekely and Dracula bloodline and its wars. On 12 May he questions Harker about business law and shipping through multiple solicitors, then makes him write letters saying he will stay a month, and warns him never to sleep outside his own rooms. Harker reads the sealed letters' addresses (Billington in Whitby, Leutner in Varna, Coutts & Co., Klopstock & Billreuth). That night he sees the Count crawl head-down down the castle wall like a lizard. On 15 May Harker forces a sagging door in the south wing, finds the old ladies' rooms, and, ignoring the warning, falls asleep there. He is visited by three vampire women; the fair one is about to bite his throat when the Count appears in fury, hurls her back and claims Harker as his own, then gives them a moving bag containing a child.

scenes.title: Realising he is a prisoner
scenes.summary: Harker rushes about trying every door, then calms and decides to keep his knowledge secret and watch.
scenes.key_quote: I behaved much as a rat does in a trap.

scenes.title: The Count does the housework
scenes.summary: Through a hinge-chink Harker watches the Count make the bed and lay the table, proving there are no servants and that the Count was the coachman. He recalls the wards given at Bistritz.
scenes.key_quote: it must have been the Count himself who was the driver of the coach that brought me here

scenes.title: The Count tells his family history
scenes.summary: Excited, the Count speaks as if he fought at every battle, tracing the Szekelys back to Attila and the Dracula voivode who beat the Turks; he pulls his moustache and grips things as if to crush them.
scenes.key_quote: What devil or what witch was ever so great as Attila, whose blood is in these veins?

scenes.title: Legal questions and the letters
scenes.summary: The Count quizzes Harker on using several solicitors for banking and shipping to Newcastle, Durham, Harwich and Dover, then insists he stay a month and write reassuring letters on thin foreign paper.

scenes.title: Spying on the letters; the warning
scenes.summary: Alone, Harker reads the addresses of four letters. The Count returns, stamps them, and warns him never to sleep in any other part of the castle.
scenes.key_quote: there are bad dreams for those who sleep unwisely. Be warned!

scenes.title: The Count crawls down the wall
scenes.location: South stone stair window; castle wall
scenes.summary: From a tall mullioned window Harker sees the Count emerge from his own window and crawl face-down down the sheer wall, cloak spread like wings, like a lizard.
scenes.key_quote: begin to crawl down the castle wall over that dreadful abyss, face down with his cloak spreading out around him like great wings

scenes.title: Exploring the castle; the great door
scenes.summary: Harker sees the Count go out again, tests all doors (new locks), finds the hall door's bolts and chains easy but the door locked with key gone, and some small rooms of moth-eaten furniture.
scenes.key_quote: the door was locked, and the key was gone!

scenes.title: The sunken door and the ladies' rooms
scenes.summary: A seemingly locked door at the top of the stairs is only jammed, its fallen hinges resting on the floor; Harker forces it and enters a suite of south and west rooms with diamond-paned windows and comfortable old furniture.
scenes.key_quote: This was evidently the portion of the castle occupied by the ladies in bygone days

scenes.title: The three women
scenes.location: The ladies' room, on a great couch
scenes.summary: Harker sleeps against the warning. Three women with no shadows appear; the fair one kneels to bite his throat. The Count seizes her neck, flings her back, claims Harker and gives them a living bag. Harker faints.

locations.name: Castle stairs and corridors
locations.description: Stone stairs and passages with many locked doors; a stairway leading up to a south-looking window.
locations.quote: I rushed up and down the stairs, trying every door and peering out of every window I could find

locations.name: South-looking stairway window
locations.description: Tall, deep, stone-mullioned window, weather-worn, no casement; below and to the left is the Count's window; the castle wall falls to an abyss.
locations.quote: The window at which I stood was tall and deep, stone-mullioned, and though weatherworn, was still complete

locations.name: Hall at the great door
locations.description: Entry hall; bolts easy to draw, chains unhooked, door locked with no key; small dusty rooms nearby with moth-eaten furniture.
locations.quote: I found I could pull back the bolts easily enough and unhook the great chains; but the door was locked

locations.name: Sagging door at the top of the stairway
locations.description: A heavy door whose fallen hinges leave it resting on the floor; opened by forcing.
locations.quote: the hinges had fallen somewhat, and the heavy door rested on the floor

locations.name: The ladies' rooms (south wing)
locations.description: Suite one storey down and further right; end room windows face west and south over precipices; diamond panes, curtainless windows, dust, moth; comfortable furniture, a little oak table, a great couch.
features: view west to jagged mountains with mountain ash and thorn
locations.quote: the yellow moonlight, flooding in through the diamond panes, enabled one to see even colours

locations.name: Castle rock and precipice
locations.description: Castle built on the corner of a great rock, impregnable on three sides, with large windows placed where sling, bow or culverin cannot reach.
locations.quote: The castle was built on the corner of a great rock, so that on three sides it was quite impregnable

characters.name: Count Dracula
characters.appearance: pulls his great white moustache; hands that grasp things as if to crush; in fury his face is deathly pale with lines like drawn wires, eyebrows like a heaving bar of white-hot metal, eyes lurid red
characters.clothing: cloak that spreads like wings when crawling
characters.personality: proud of his bloodline, devious, jealous of Harker
characters.speech_style: uses 'we' like a king; courteous threats
notable_lines: How dare you touch him, any of you? ... This man belongs to me!
abilities: climbs head-down down sheer wall like a lizard
commands the women with a gesture

characters.name: Three vampire women (the weird sisters)
characters.appearance: three young women who cast no shadow in moonlight; two dark with high aquiline noses and great piercing eyes that seem red; one fair with wavy golden hair and pale sapphire-blue eyes (Harker half-recognises her); brilliant white teeth, ruby voluptuous lips
characters.speech_style: silvery laughter 'like water-glasses played by a cunning hand'
notable_lines: Go on! You are first, and we shall follow; yours is the right to begin.
He is young and strong; there are kisses for us all.
You yourself never loved; you never love!
Are we to have nothing to-night?
abilities: fade into moonbeams and pass out the window

objects.name: Crucifix over the bed head
objects.description: Placed over the head of Harker's bed.
objects.quote: I have placed the crucifix over the head of my bed

objects.name: Writing paper and envelopes
objects.description: Three sheets of thinnest foreign post and three envelopes given by the Count.
objects.quote: three sheets of note-paper and three envelopes. They were all of the thinnest foreign post

objects.name: The four letters
objects.description: Addressed to Samuel F. Billington, No. 7, The Crescent, Whitby; Herr Leutner, Varna; Coutts & Co., London; Herren Klopstock & Billreuth, bankers, Buda-Pesth. Second and fourth unsealed.
objects.quote: directed to Samuel F. Billington, No. 7, The Crescent, Whitby, another to Herr Leutner, Varna

objects.name: Harker's diary in shorthand
objects.description: His journal and pen kept in a pocket.
objects.quote: I had fortunately replaced the book and pen in my pocket

objects.name: Lamp
objects.description: Lamp Harker takes to try all the doors; pale against moonlight.
objects.quote: taking a lamp, tried all the doors

objects.name: Hall door key (missing)
objects.description: Key to the great hall door, taken away; Harker suspects it is in the Count's room.
objects.quote: That key must be in the Count’s room

objects.name: Small oak table
objects.description: Little oak table where a lady might have written love-letters.
objects.quote: sitting at a little oak table where in old times possibly some fair lady sat to pen

objects.name: Great couch
objects.description: Heavy couch Harker drags near the corner to look east and south.
objects.quote: I drew a great couch out of its place near the corner

objects.name: The bag
objects.description: A bag thrown on the floor that moves with a living thing inside; a child's wail is heard when opened.
objects.function_in_story: Feeding the women with a child.
objects.quote: the bag which he had thrown upon the floor, and which moved as though there were some living thing within it

objects.name: Garlic, wild rose, mountain ash
objects.description: Named as items the peasants gave Harker.
objects.quote: What meant the giving of the crucifix, of the garlic, of the wild rose, of the mountain ash?

creatures.name: Three vampire women
creatures.description: Beautiful women with no shadow, red-seeming eyes and pearl-white teeth; they lick lips and hover over the victim.
creatures.behaviour: Approach a sleeper, argue over who goes first, prefer a throat bite; obey the Count's authority; take a child in a bag.
creatures.quote: though the moonlight was behind them, they threw no shadow on the floor

creatures.name: Count Dracula as wall-crawler
creatures.description: Crawls head-down down the sheer castle wall, fingers and toes gripping eroded stones.
creatures.behaviour: Leaves the castle at night by his window, vanishes into a lower hole.
creatures.quote: just as a lizard moves along a wall

creatures.name: Child in the bag
creatures.description: A smothered child heard wailing in the bag.
creatures.quote: a gasp and a low wail, as of a half-smothered child

vampire_lore.detail: The three women cast no shadow in bright moonlight.
vampire_lore.quote: they threw no shadow on the floor

vampire_lore.rule: Bite at the throat; sweet breath tinged with blood
vampire_lore.detail: The fair woman's breath is honey-sweet with a bitter blood smell.
vampire_lore.quote: a bitter offensiveness, as one smells in blood

vampire_lore.detail: Harker feels desire and awaits the kiss.
vampire_lore.quote: a wicked, burning desire that they would kiss me

vampire_lore.detail: They fade into the moonbeams and pass through the window.
vampire_lore.quote: They simply seemed to fade into the rays of the moonlight

vampire_lore.detail: The Count descends sheer walls head-first.
vampire_lore.quote: just as a lizard moves along a wall

vampire_lore.rule: Sleeping outside the Count's rooms is dangerous
vampire_lore.detail: The Count warns Harker not to sleep elsewhere or there will be bad dreams (washing-hands gesture).
vampire_lore.quote: you will not by any chance go to sleep in any other part of the castle

vampire_lore.detail: Harker feels comfort and freer rest with it over his bed.
vampire_lore.quote: it is a comfort and a strength to me whenever I touch it

vampire_lore.detail: His gesture drives the women back as it did the wolves.
vampire_lore.quote: it was the same imperious gesture that I had seen used to the wolves

vampire_lore.detail: The women are given a bag with a living child.
vampire_lore.quote: Are we to have nothing to-night?

vampire_lore.rule: The Count's eyes glow red in anger
vampire_lore.quote: The red light in them was lurid, as if the flames of hell-fire blazed behind them.

vampire_lore.detail: The Count's work is at night; Harker's own routine is being destroyed.

puzzles.name: Hinge-sagging door
puzzles.setup: A door at the top of the stairway seems locked.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker recognises the fallen hinges and forces it by repeated effort.
puzzles.game_idea: Physics puzzle: lift or wedge a sagging door to move it past its dropped hinges.
puzzles.quote: it was not really locked, but that the resistance came from the fact that the hinges had fallen somewhat

puzzles.name: Hall door with key missing
puzzles.setup: Bolts and chains easy but door locked.
puzzles.book_solution: Not solved; Harker infers the key is in the Count's room.
puzzles.quote: the door was locked, and the key was gone!

puzzles.name: Reading letters undetected
puzzles.book_solution: Read addresses and replace them as found when the door-handle moves.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth puzzle with a timer: read as many addresses as possible and restore state before the door opens.
puzzles.quote: I had just time to replace the letters as they had been

puzzles.name: Hidden writing
puzzles.obstacle: Harker needs to warn people secretly.
puzzles.book_solution: Writes formal notes openly and uses shorthand for Mina.
puzzles.game_idea: Cipher puzzle: communicate only via a code the villain cannot read.
puzzles.quote: to her I could write in shorthand, which would puzzle the Count

puzzles.name: Observing the wall-crawl
puzzles.setup: Watching the Count from the stair window.
puzzles.obstacle: Angle of sight; he vanishes into a hole.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker watches from behind the stone mullion, then tries leaning out.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth observation: hide behind stonework to track the Count's route.
puzzles.quote: I drew back behind the stonework, and looked carefully out.

combat.name: Three women vs sleeping Harker
combat.tactics: Harker is passive/entranced; the Count intervenes by force.
combat.outcome: Harker is saved by the Count for his own purposes and faints.
combat.game_idea: Resist-the-charm scenario: each turn a willpower check against enthrallment; the Count appears as a scripted deus ex machina or player must use the crucifix.
combat.quote: I closed my eyes in a languorous ecstasy and waited

quest_hooks: Find the key to the hall door (probably in Dracula's room).
Do not sleep outside your own rooms: obey or disobey the warning.
Secretly write to Mina in shorthand; hide the letter.
Watch the Count's night routes from the south window.
Survive the encounter with the three women using willpower and the crucifix.
